We present the entire scheme-independent dynamical response $\bar{F}_{\ell,s}$ of a Schwarzschild black hole in closed form, to all orders in $G$, and for every spin $s$ and multipole $\ell$. The result is $\bar{F}_{\ell,s}/4\pi R_S^{2\ell+1}=\Phi_{\ell,s}(\bar{y})-\tfrac12\eta\,\Phi_{\ell,s}'(\bar{y})$ with $\bar{y}=-\tfrac12\eta^2\tau$ and $\eta=i\omega R_S$. Here $\Phi_{\ell,s}$ is simply the leading-log solution to the renormalization group equation, but lifting the running logarithm to $\tau=\log(R_S/R)-2\sum_{k\ge2}\zeta_k\,\eta^{k-1}$ resums it to all orders. This tower of Riemann zeta values is the Newtonian phase in disguise: it originates from the long-range $1/r$ potential in the far zone, and is universal across multipole and spin. Our result exhibits a factorization pinned to three ingredients: the strength of horizon absorption, the running rate in the near zone, and the dressed logarithm in the far zone. Using shell effective field theory, we independently verify our formula for scalar, electromagnetic, and gravitational perturbations, reaching $\mathcal O(G^{15})$.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail P. Solon (UCLA)

item.title: Revisiting the Wess-Zumino-Witten Term in Nuclear and Quark Matter under Magnetic Fields and Rotation
item.description: arXiv:2607.04929v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study anomalous Wess-Zumino-Witten terms associated with the chiral anomaly in dense QCD matter under magnetic fields and rotation. By introducing electromagnetic, baryon number, and isospin background gauge fields, we write down the topological couplings of neutral mesons for the $N_f=2$ and $N_f=3$ cases. The resulting terms contain characteristic contributions proportional to $\vec{B} \cdot \vec{\nabla} \phi$ and $\vec{\Omega} \cdot \vec{\nabla} \phi$, where $\phi$ denotes $\pi^0$, $\eta$, or $\eta'$. These results are relevant to chiral soliton lattices in dense rotating matter.
item.dc:creator: Markus A. G. Amano, Minoru Eto, Muneto Nitta, Shin Sasaki

item.title: Quantum Field Theory Of Cosmological Perturbations Induced By Ultralight Dark Matter
item.description: arXiv:2607.27133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The growth of primordial perturbations during the matter-dominated era is primarily driven by dark matter. Ultralight scalar fields (ULDM) are a promising candidate for this role, conventionally modeled as operating in a classical, high-occupation regime. In this work, we develop a first-principles field-theoretic framework to investigate the impact of ULDM on linear cosmological perturbations during matter domination, explicitly retaining its quantum nature. Deriving a closed equation for the graviton field dynamics, we compute and regularize its source terms for a generic Gaussian initial state of the ULDM field within the adiabatic (WKB) approximation, employing the middle-point working assumption for non-local terms. After gauge-fixing we find that, contrary to previous claims, the classical condensate of ULDM has no influence on gravitational wave propagation. However, the time-dependent graviton effective mass induced by quantum pressure of the squeezed state can drive parametric resonance in specific primordial gravitational wave modes. We demonstrate this growth is negligible for non-relativistic ULDM at matter-radiation equality under the assumption of a power-law squeezing spectrum for masses in the range $m \sim 10^{-21}{-}10^{-24}$ eV.
item.dc:creator: Tomislav Prokopec, Marco Vecchioni

item.title: Genus-One Rigidity of Bounded Virasoro Pairings for 3D Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2608.03459v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study whether varying the topological boundary of the doubled Virasoro TQFT can produce distinct torus pairings for an ensemble interpretation of 3D gravity. In the ordinary nondegenerate sector, every bounded pairing that commutes with the modular transformations is scalar, and vacuum normalization selects the diagonal pairing. The proof identifies the modular transformations with the even Weil representation and applies the Cowling--Steger lattice-restriction theorem. Under the ordinary block-diagonal vacuum--continuum ansatz, positivity and the two vacuum marginals also make a Borel-measure pairing bounded, without assuming absolute continuity; modular invariance then forces the same diagonal pairing. These two classes therefore contain no distinct torus pairings to average. A nontrivial Virasoro boundary ensemble must involve genus-one data outside these classes, additional sectors or vacuum--continuum couplings, or information invisible in the torus pairing. Elementary proofs in explicit regular sectors explain the rigidity mechanisms, and numerical calculations provide independent checks.
item.dc:creator: Xingyang Yu

item.title: Tripartite Form Universality in Holographic Entropy Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2609.22504v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To elucidate the meaning of holographic entropy inequalities (beyond subadditivity) which characterize the entanglement structure of geometric states in holography, arXiv:2309.06296 proposed the "tripartite form" for these inequalities, consisting of tripartite information and conditional tripartite information terms with unit coefficients. While this provides a compact and useful packaging of the inequalities, it is not a priori guaranteed that all inequalities can be recast in this form. Here we conjecture that they can, and present substantial evidence, by proving that the two known infinite families of holographic entropy inequalities found in arXiv:2309.15145 can indeed be written in the tripartite form. This is significant because such recasting is particularly nontrivial for these families. Apart from providing the explicit tripartite form expressions for every member of these two infinite families, we detail how we arrived at them, in the process deriving several useful identities which may serve as stepping stones to formulate further repackaging of the corresponding information quantities. We also illustrate the power of the tripartite form by proving a number of structural properties satisfied by any holographic entropy inequality.
item.dc:creator: Veronika E. Hubeny, Yu Liu

item.title: Numerical Sasaki--Einstein metrics and harmonic forms on del Pezzo links
item.description: arXiv:2609.25857v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We numerically construct the Sasaki--Einstein metric on the link of the cone over the second del Pezzo surface $\mathrm{dP}_2$ and two primitive harmonic basic $(1,1)$-forms at its irregular volume-minimizing Reeb vector. Being toric, the metric in symplectic coordinates is encoded in a single convex function on a polygon. We approximate the correction to the canonical Guillemin potential in two ways: polynomial expansion and neural networks. The polynomial fit achieves a held-out mean-squared Monge--Amp\`ere residual below $10^{-13}$, in contrast to the $10^{-2}$ plateau for the non-volume-minimizing regular Reeb vector. We validate our method against closed-form metrics of $Y^{p,q}$ using curvature invariants, and also against the numerical result of Doran et al. (2007) for the K\"ahler--Einstein metric of $\mathrm{dP}_3$ using the Laplacian spectrum of low torus-invariant modes. The integrated Riemann-squared curvature of the $\mathrm{dP}_2$ link agrees to two parts in $10^{9}$ with the closed form conjectured from the dual field theory. Our data for the metric and harmonic forms can be used to study warped non-conformal holographic IIB backgrounds, the analogues of the Klebanov--Tseytlin solution on the conifold.
item.dc:creator: Nakwoo Kim, Sejin Kim, Hoseob Shin

item.title: Coherent Release Fronts in Krylov Chains and Thermal AdS$_2$ Response
item.description: arXiv:2610.01862v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study coherent release from a finite serial Krylov sector into an exact conformal tail with asymptotically linear Lanczos coefficients. We derive the cumulative occupation up to a cut that moves to greater Krylov depth with time, tracking the probability accumulated behind the propagating front. This quantity separates the release dynamics of the finite sector from subsequent propagation through the tail. The tail sets the logarithmic transit scale, while the finite sector shapes the resulting distribution. The early edge records the number of serial steps before emission, while the late edge reflects slow resonances and interference and can also exhibit logarithmic enhancements. Thus, one- and two-site sectors can share the same leading resonance in their continued-fraction descriptions yet produce distinct cumulative occupation patterns. We illustrate this framework in thermal AdS$_2$, where a dressed oscillator yields, in the weak-coupling limit, a two-site shallow sector coupled to the conformal tail.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Alishahiha

item.title: Conformal Anomalies and Generalised Energy Conservation in De Sitter Spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2610.08113v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that for bulk discrete series fields whose dual operators have integer conformal dimensions, the Generalised Energy Conservation (GEC) condition for de Sitter (dS) scattering amplitudes defined in even-dimensional extended Poincar\'e spacetime corresponds precisely to the absence of boundary conformal anomalies, including beta-function contributions, at the level of tree-level contact interactions. In contrast, holographic consistency in AdS/CFT enforces only the locality of the conformal anomaly. We find novel, unique four-point interactions involving three identical conformally coupled scalars and one discrete series scalar by performing both GEC and holographic bootstraps. This demonstrates that the solutions to GEC form a measure-zero subset of the holographically consistent solutions. Our holographic analysis agrees precisely with the expected renormalisation conditions for conformal field theory correlators. In addition, the constraint for a particular four-point configuration may be relevant for testing holographic consistency of scale-separated non-supersymmetric AdS$_4$ vacua.
item.dc:creator: Zong-Zhe Du

item.title: Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight
item.description: arXiv:2610.14441v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. It is generated by two commuting affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ current algebras at levels $1$ and $39$, the stress tensor of the lattice theory, and a single weight-two field built from three lattice exponentials. We announce that $U$ is strongly rational and completely unitary, and that $Rep(U)$ is equivalent, as a unitary ribbon category, to the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category $\mathcal{H}_3$. Its characters are the $\gamma=0$ Evans--Gannon vector. From $U$ we obtain a diagonal full CFT, and also a holomorphic $E_8$ extension on which $\mathcal{H}_3$ acts by topological defects.
item.dc:creator: Tzu-Chen Huang

item.title: KP integrability of non-perturbative differentials
item.description: arXiv:2412.18592v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the KP integrability of non-perturbative topological recursion, which can be considered as a formal $\hbar$-deformation of the Krichever construction of algebro-geometric solutions of the KP hierarchy. This property goes back to a 2011 conjecture of Borot and Eynard.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal de l'\'Ecole polytechnique -- Math\'ematiques, Volume 13 (2026), pp. 1607-1635
item.dc:creator: Alexander Alexandrov, Boris Bychkov, Petr Dunin-Barkowski, Maxim Kazarian, Sergey Shadrin

item.title: All toric Hermitian ALE gravitational instantons
item.description: arXiv:2510.09291v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the only smooth, Ricci flat, ALE gravitational instanton with a toric Hermitian non-K\"ahler structure is the Eguchi-Hanson instanton. The proof is analogous to the classification of toric Hermitian ALF instantons by Biquard and Gauduchon, although we avoid the use of toric K\"ahler geometry and instead perform a direct global analysis of the Tod form of the metric in Weyl-Papapetrou coordinates. This supports a conjecture by Gibbons and Bando-Kasue-Nakajima which states that any Ricci flat ALE instanton is self-dual.
item.dc:creator: Bernardo Araneda, James Lucietti

item.title: Isotensor $\pi\pi \pi$ scattering with a $\rho$ resonant subsystem from QCD
item.description: arXiv:2510.24894v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This work presents a lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) determination of $\pi\pi\pi$ scattering amplitudes for the isospin-2 channel with angular momentum and parity $J^{P} = 1^+$. The calculation is performed using unphysically heavy light-quark masses, corresponding to a pion mass of $m_{\pi} \approx 400$~MeV, for which the $\rho$ meson manifests as a narrow resonance. The analysis employs a previously developed formalism that non-perturbatively relates the finite-volume spectra of two- and three-pion systems to their infinite-volume scattering amplitudes. We combine earlier lattice QCD results for $\pi\pi$ systems with isospins 1 and 2 with new determinations of the isospin-2 three-pion finite-volume spectrum, obtained for three cubic, periodic lattice volumes with box lengths ranging from $\approx 4/m_\pi$ to $6/m_\pi$. These combined data constrain the low-lying partial waves of the infinite-volume three-pion K matrix, from which we solve a set of coupled integral equations to extract the corresponding scattering amplitudes.
item.dc:creator: Ra\'ul A. Brice\~no, Maxwell T. Hansen, Andrew W. Jackura, Robert G. Edwards, Christopher E. Thomas

item.title: Cluster algebra and quasimap quantum cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2511.09875v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We apply the abelianization technique to obtain an explicit ring presentation for the quasimap quantum cohomology of GIT quotients. As an application, for quiver varieties associated with oriented-acyclic quivers, we establish a cluster algebra structure on their equivariant quasimap quantum cohomology rings.
item.dc:creator: Yingchun Zhang, Zijun Zhou

item.title: Dirac Observables for Gowdy Cosmologies Regular at the Big Bang
item.description: arXiv:2602.03663v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gowdy cosmologies are exact, spatially inhomogeneous solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations which describe nonlinear gravitational waves coalescing at the big bang singularity. With toroidal spatial sections they provenly have the asymptotic velocity domination property, in that close to the big bang dynamical spatial gradients fade out and the dynamics is governed by a Carroll-type gravity theory. Here we construct an infinite set of exact Dirac observables for Gowdy cosmologies, valid off-shell, strongly, and without gauge fixing. These observables stay regular at the big bang and can be matched to much simpler Dirac observables of the Carroll-type gravity theory. Conversely, in an adapted foliation there is a systematic anti-Newtonian expansion (in inverse powers of the reduced Newton constant) of the full Dirac observables whose leading terms are the Carroll ones. In particular, this provides an off-shell generalization of the asymptotic velocity domination property.
item.dc:creator: Max Niedermaier, Mahdi Sedighi Jafari

item.title: Probing scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves in the nHz band: NANOGrav and SKA
item.description: arXiv:2604.13012v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) have recently attracted considerable interest, both as a possible explanation for the nanohertz signal reported by the Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) collaboration and for their connection with primordial black hole (PBH) physics. In addition to SIGWs, scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves (STGWs) have emerged as a promising cosmological source of the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB). In this paper, we compute the STGWs generated during a generic matter-dominated (MD) era, as well as during an early matter-dominated (eMD) epoch followed by a sudden transition to the standard radiation-dominated (RD) stage, working in the Poisson gauge. We find that, in a purely MD age, the corresponding energy density rapidly dilutes, whereas in the presence of an eMD phase it remains non-vanishing due to the short duration of the eMD period. We then investigate whether the STGW signal could provide a dominant contribution to the \texttt{NANOGrav 15-year} dataset and we forecast the prospects for its detection with future observations by the Square Kilometre Array (SKA). In particular, we consider STGWs generated during both eMD and RD eras, including their linear-order contributions. We further inject the scalar-induced contribution, both as an additional component and as the only signal, and compare the spectra against the same datasets. Our results show that, although the SIGWs still appear to provide the dominant contribution and the posteriors are tightly constrained by the requirement of avoiding PBH overproduction, the GWs induced by scalar-tensor mixing constitute a viable target for future, more sensitive nano-Hz detectors of the SGWB.
item.dc:creator: William Iania, Angelo Ricciardone

item.title: The Spurion Massive EFT (SMEFT)
item.description: arXiv:2604.14274v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use the amplitude formulation of the SMEFT to introduce a spurion analysis of the SMEFT low-energy amplitudes in terms of the Higgs VEV. Each SMEFT contact-term is given as a sum of a few spurion structures, whose number depends on the electroweak charges of the external legs. The coefficients of these structures involve singlet combinations of Higgses from higher-order SMEFT contributions. We use this to derive the spurion expansions of the W- and Z-boson masses and mixing, and their three-point couplings to fermions. The textures of these couplings are saturated by the dimension-eight SMEFT. Our analysis can be generalized to higher-point amplitudes and nonzero Yukawa couplings.
item.dc:creator: Julian L. Northey, Yael Shadmi, Yotam Soreq, Daiki Ueda

item.title: Hyperstatistics
item.description: arXiv:2604.24783v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a general approach, named by us hyperstatistics, to treat complex systems, in which Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics breaks down at the domain level of the system. Hyperstatistics preserves the concavity of the nonadditive $q$-entropy. We obtain analytical closed-form expressions for the here proposed ($q, n$)-generalized Boltzmann factor $B_q^{n}$ considering uniform, $\gamma$, Log-normal, F, and the $q$-$\gamma$ probability distribution functions. Remarkably, for all investigated distribution functions, $B_q^{n}$ reduces to a $q$-exponential-type function. To demonstrate the applicability of hyperstatistics, we use a table top experiment of the discharge of a capacitor considering $\gamma$-distributed relaxation times, the pressure decay over time associated with the pumping of $^4$He lines of a closed cycle cryostat, midrapidity data for $\textit{p}$-Pb collisions at the LHC, as well as data set for acceleration distribution in turbulent systems. Furthermore, we deduce the power-law-like $\textit{universal}$ dielectric response using a $q$-generalized $\gamma$-distribution function proposed in this work. Hyperstatistics is applicable to systems with inherent non-Boltzmann-Gibbsian statistics at the domain level. We demonstrate that at the domain level hyperstatistics and superstatistics are equivalent, while at the macroscopic level hyperstatistics recovers superstatistics for $q \to 1$ because the Boltzmann-Gibbs character of the domains is restored, as well as Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics for $n \to \infty$.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Squillante, Samuel M. Soares, Constantino Tsallis, Mariano de Souza

item.title: Expanding quantum magnetic field
item.description: arXiv:2605.27426v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop the quantum theory of the causal formation of a long-range magnetic field generated by an external current that is instantaneously switched on and subsequently kept constant in time. The resulting non-equilibrium quantum state, describing the expanding magnetic field, is obtained exactly and compared with the corresponding quantum magnetostatic state. In contrast to the magnetostatic case, the expanding solution exhibits a propagating shockwave-like front separating regions where the magnetic field has already been formed from those that remain causally disconnected from the source. We show that although the expanding field locally approaches the magnetostatic field behind the shockwave-like front, the associated quantum systems remain distinct at all times. In particular, we obtain manifestly different results for the energy, photon number, and their fluctuations in expanding and magnetostatic field configurations. Our results are first derived for a general external current and then illustrated with a specific example.
item.dc:creator: Bogdan Damski

item.title: Time-reversed stochastic inflation in the quantum well
item.description: arXiv:2605.31323v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Time-reversed stochastic inflation solves the stochastic evolution of the inflationary universe backward in time, by counting the number of e-folds from the end of quantum diffusion towards some initial state. The point of view of observers attached to the end-of-inflation hypersurface is thus enforced. In this work, we exactly solve time-reversed stochastic inflation in a flat and bounded potential, the so-called quantum well. At given lifetime, the field behaviour is found to be either indistinguishable from the one obtained in a semi-infinite flat potential, or, subject to enhanced stochasticity where any memory of the initial state is erased. The derived distribution of curvature perturbations reduces to the semi-infinite result for small fluctuations while it develops exponential tails for the large ones. Such tails arise for both positive and negative values, and decay twice as fast as the one obtained in the standard forward stochastic inflation. These differences may have important consequences for tail-sensitive phenomena, such as primordial black hole formation.
item.dc:creator: Chiara Animali, Baptiste Blachier, Nanoka Okada, Christophe Ringeval, Tomo Takahashi, Koki Tokeshi

item.title: On the Renormalization Group Flow of Active Flocks
item.description: arXiv:2606.20552v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the statistical field-theoretic renormalization of active flocks via the Martin-Siggia-Rose-De Dominicis-Janssen (MSRDJ) formulation of stochastic dynamics, focusing on the Toner-Tu theory of Malthusian flocks, or polar-ordered, momentum non-conserving active fluids in which density fluctuations relax sufficiently rapidly to be eliminated as hydrodynamic degrees of freedom. Working in the limit of isotropic diffusion in two spatial dimensions, we perform an all orders analysis of the perturbative renormalization of propagators and interaction vertices. We show that a nonlinearly realized diagonal rotation/shift symmetry gives rise to Ward identities that protect the trigonometric structure of the convective derivative, ensuring that the sine and cosine interaction potentials retain their functional form under renormalization up to a rescaling of their overall couplings. We demonstrate that the freedom to renormalize the dynamical critical exponent in this boost non-invariant theory prevents the determination of the precise values of the critical exponents and anomalous dimensions in the theory, highlighting parallels and crucial differences with sine-Gordon and XY models. We express all anomalous dimensions as functions of the dynamical critical exponent, which remains undetermined due to the absence of a relation ordinarily forced upon boost invariant systems. We revisit and contextualize several claims and counterclaims in the recent literature in light of these results.
item.dc:creator: Kevin T. Grosvenor, Subodh P. Patil

item.title: Soft-Radiation-Induced Decoherence of Heavy-Quark Spin Entanglement at the Electron-Ion Collider
item.description: arXiv:2606.29944v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using the soft-gluon theorem, we identify a soft-recoil mechanism by which unresolved gluon radiation induces decoherence in the spin correlations of heavy quark-antiquark pairs produced by longitudinally polarized virtual photons in deep-inelastic scattering. Upon tracing over the unresolved gluon, the reduced spin density matrix is block diagonal in the mirror parity of the production plane and is governed by two coefficients: a parity-odd normal-spin flip, which reduces the normal-axis correlation, and a parity-even stochastic rotation of the spin-correlation plane about its normal, which suppresses the in-plane spin coherences while leaving the normal-axis correlation unchanged. From the complete tree-level next-to-soft amplitude with the exact color-octet structure we derive both coefficients, together with the trace and antisymmetric in-plane terms, in closed form. The parity-odd coefficient is the larger one, by a factor of at least $3.5$, and grows as the inverse square of the heavy-quark transverse momentum. We estimate the resulting reduction of concurrence and Bell-CHSH violation, and propose an infrared-safe, radiation-binned EIC observable, formed at fixed Born kinematics after longitudinal-transverse separation, which isolates the two channels. We estimate its size, including multiple wide-angle emissions in an independent-emission model, the conditions under which detector and kinematic effects cancel, and the statistics required. The latter, however, exceed the yield of exclusive heavy-baryon pairs at nominal EIC luminosity by several orders of magnitude, makes the observable elusive for the measurement accessible in that channel.

item.title: Ghosts that Connect
item.description: arXiv:2607.27297v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: What is a Faddeev--Popov ghost? The textbook answer is that it is a trick: a way of writing a functional determinant as a term in the action, and nothing more. Dougherty 2021 and Dougherty and Read 2026 have argued that this undersells the ghost, which on their account encodes classical structure of the configuration space, viz. the degree-one generators of the Chevalley--Eilenberg complex of the action Lie algebroid. I agree with them that the ghost encodes classical structure. But I think the structure is bigger than they say. The ghost, I argue, is a principal connection $\varpi$ on the bundle $F \to F/G$ of gauge potentials over physical configurations; the BRST operator is the exterior derivative along the orbits; and the Chevalley--Eilenberg ghost coincides with $\varpi$ restricted to the orbits (and every $\varpi$ has the same restriction). The restriction drops the horizontal complement, and I show that gauge-fixed quantisation needs that complement. A gauge-fixing installs it as a pairing of configurations across orbits (a counterpart relation, in Lewis's sense); dressed observables and local counterfactuals rely on this pairing, but it is discarded by the quotient $\F/\G$. In the non-Abelian case Singer's theorem forbids a flat $\varpi$, and there the pairing exists only as parallel transport. Finally, BRST survives gauge-fixing because it is vertical and rigid, and so leaves any such pairing unchanged.

item.title: Complex chromoelectric polarizability of a heavy-quarkonium resonance: pole response and channel-resolved effective-theory representation
item.description: arXiv:2608.00611v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a stable compact quarkonium state in the pNRQCD multipole regime, chromoelectric polarizability arises at leading order from two E1 transitions through virtual color-octet states. For an unstable state, we define the corresponding response through the quadratic displacement of its complex resonance pole in a weak chromoelectric background, so that its real and imaginary parts describe field-induced shifts of the pole mass and width. Starting from a renormalized background-field correlator, we show that the resonance polarizability is given by the complete two-field kernel normalized by the energy derivative of the full inverse propagator at the pole. In an effective theory with explicitly separated intermediate sectors, the kernel contains the standard E1-octet-E1 contribution, the complete source response of decay channels already coupled at zero field, and local contributions. This distinction becomes essential above open-flavor threshold and reduces to the standard pNRQCD polarizability in the stable, energy-independent limit. A simple $D\bar D$ realization for the $\psi(3770)$ gives the complex pole-residue factor $1/[1-\sigma'(z_\psi)]=0.800-0.336$, illustrating that threshold dressing can substantially modify both the magnitude and phase of the response. The resulting pole-based relation identifies the quantity required for a source-dependent coupled-channel determination of the chromoelectric polarizability of a heavy-quarkonium resonance.

item.title: Classical soft theorems meet the post-Newtonian expansion
item.description: arXiv:2609.29895v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Classical soft theorems govern the non-analytic structure of electromagnetic and gravitational radiation in the low-frequency regime, with the gravitational memory effect providing the canonical realization of the classical soft graviton theorem. While the soft behavior of radiation from hyperbolic scattering is well understood, its realization in gravitationally bound systems remains less explored. In this work, we study the soft structure of gravitational waveforms generated by compact binaries, focusing on the scattering of emitted radiation off the static background curvature within the multipolar post-Newtonian framework. We isolate the infrared (IR) logarithms associated with hereditary effects, including the tail-of-memory, and their higher generalizations with n-tail insertions. The resulting amplitudes exhibit a Laurent expansion in frequency space consistent with the Sahoo-Sen logarithmic soft theorems, thereby establishing a direct correspondence between gravitational memory effects, their higher-order tail corrections, and the soft expansion. We also comment on ultraviolet (UV) logarithms arising from short-distance sensitivity of the multipole expansion and their associated renormalization-group running.

item.title: Stability and Formation of Solitonic Boson Stars
item.description: arXiv:2609.30021v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend a previous study of the radial stability of solitonic boson stars by nonlinearly evolving them under aspherical perturbations, and by studying their formation from the collapse of scalar clouds. We focus in particular on models previously identified as radially stable, despite having positive binding energy, which ordinarily suggests that dispersion of all scalar matter is energetically preferred. A mode analysis of our 3+1 evolutions produces no evidence for the presence of a non-radial instability in any radially stable model, including those with positive binding energy. However, we do find evidence that such models do not generically form via gravitational cooling. We also find that it is possible to form another kind of compact object, which undergoes long-lasting radial oscillations and hence cannot be described as a stationary boson star. These objects may be characterized, we suggest, by energetically favoured multi-oscillating solutions to the Einstein-Klein-Gordon equations, present in certain regions of the parameter space.

item.title: Safety of dynamical SUSY breaking and gaugino condensation in models of spontaneous CP violation
item.description: arXiv:2610.08002v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Solving the strong CP problem with spontaneous CP violation (SCPV) in SUSY requires that the constant term of the superpotential and the SUSY-breaking F-term be real to high accuracy. When both are generated dynamically, by gaugino condensation and by dynamical SUSY breaking (DSB), their phases need not vanish even if every theta-angle vanishes and every coupling is real; e.g., the multivalued non-perturbative superpotential may sit on a branch with a complex phase. In fact, gaugino condensation, in pure SUSY Yang-Mills theory and in its Affleck-Dine-Seiberg generalization, is safe only for N_c - N_f in {1,2} (N_c = 2 for pure SYM); otherwise the phase of the constant term reaches the gluino mass through anomaly mediation. The SUSY-breaking F-term is the main source of the MSSM soft masses, including the gluino mass, so its phase reaches theta-bar as well. In the framework of global SUSY, the 3-2 model introduces no phase. The ISS model is safe in that sector as long as the quark-mass splittings exceed the messenger-loop corrections; when they fall below, a complex vacuum orientation can generate an O(1) phase. The IYIT model can generate a purely imaginary F-term: for half of the real Yukawa parameter space, the meson VEV is purely imaginary and CP is spontaneously broken. In all three, the vacuum of the field coupled to the messengers is aligned with the constant term, so a complex constant term generates a strong CP phase through a second route, separate from anomaly mediation.
